page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-32GB is an x86_64 virtual server instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. It is equipped with 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.67 GB of memory per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage and includes no discrete graphics hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements place the instance within the mid-range tier for sustained multi-threaded compute and data handling tasks. It achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,817.0 and a single-core score of 2,199.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 22,297.86. Memory subsystem performance reached 54.21 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 42.64 GB/sec on writes. In application benchmarks, the server handled 17.5 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 9.33 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language model inference shows capacity for small models, producing 107.09 text tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, though throughput drops to 4.94 tokens per second on a medium 7B parameter model.

Because the 12 vCPUs run on a shared allocation model, this instance provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded batch operations and parallel workloads that do not demand dedicated hardware threads. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates attaching network storage volumes for stateful execution. The configuration is suitable for distributed microservices, application backends, container orchestration nodes, multi-threaded compilation tasks, and web serving.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-32GB is a KVM-based virtual server featuring 12 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system RAM. Architecture utilizes x86_64 instruction sets, providing 2.67 GB of memory per vCPU core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and no GPU hardware. Synthetic testing demonstrates moderate throughput, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,817.0, a PassMark CPU score of 22,297.86, and Redis throughput of 17.5 million SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 54.21 GB/sec on large read transfers. Due to its shared core structure and lean memory-to-core allocation, the instance delivers practical resource density for parallel tasks. It is well matched for containerized microservices, multi-threaded build jobs, web hosting layers, and stateless API servers.
